label: soundness-checked, PROTOTYPE, PENDING CRYPTO AUDIT

evidence.missing_capability: No snarkjs command for proof folding, proof aggregation, or recursive proof composition was present in the local CLI help.
evidence.circomlib_search: Local circomlib circuits include poseidon, bitify, comparators, eddsa, smt, sha256, and related primitives, but no Groth16 verifier, pairing verifier, Miller loop, final exponentiation, or recursive aggregation circuit template.
evidence.repo_search: Repository search found Solidity Groth16 verifier code and stubs, not a circuit-level verifier suitable for recursive aggregation.

why_no_fake_aggregate: An aggregate proof must genuinely attest all N sub-proofs. Hashing N proof files together or verifying one representative proof would not be recursive proof composition and would be fake security.
what_would_be_required: A circuit-level verifier for the chosen proof system, or a zkVM/STARK recursion stack with supported proof aggregation.
A setup large enough for the recursive verifier circuit if using Groth16-in-Groth16.
Tests where one invalid sub-proof makes the aggregate fail, a swapped sub-proof fails, and claimed N cannot differ from the actual sub-proof count.
External cryptographic audit before production use.
conclusion: Aggregation path is cloud/audit-track in this local environment. Phase 1 multi-claim circuit is the more production-suitable local path today.
